q-79607.name: Question 1
q-79607.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=x,{f}_{1}=-1,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =(x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})\frac{1}{x} \\  & =x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\frac{1}{x})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})-(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =x\cdot (\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

q-79607.html:
Question 1
?

Given that D=xd2dx2−ddx, what is D(y) for y=1x?

a
1x3
b
−2x3
c
3x2
d
−1x2
e
2x2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=f2(x)d2ydx2+f1(x)dydx+f0(x)y with f2=x,f1=−1, and f0=0.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y:

D(y)=D(1x)=(xd2dx2−ddx)1x=xd2dx2(1x)−ddx(1x)=xddx(−1x2)−(−1x2)=x⋅(2x3)+1x2=2x2+1x2=3x2

q-130248.name: Question 2
q-130248.worked_solution:
The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{3}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y.
$$

with ${f}_{3}={x}^{2},{f}_{2}=3x,{f}_{1}=-1,$ and ${f}_{0}=0.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =({x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+3x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}(\frac{1}{x})+3x\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\frac{1}{x})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})+3x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})-(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & ={x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})+3x(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{6}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

q-130248.html:
Question 2
?

Given that D=x2d3dx3+3xd2dx2−ddx, what is D(y) for y=1x?

a
−1x
b
4x
c
2
d
1x2
e
−2x2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form D(y)=f3(x)d3ydx3+f2(x)d2ydx2+f1(x)dydx+f0(x)y. with f3=x2,f2=3x,f1=−1, and f0=0.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y:

D(y)=D(1x)=(x2d3dx3+3xd2dx2−ddx)(1x)=x2d3dx3(1x)+3xd2dx2(1x)−ddx(1x)=x2d2dx2(−1x2)+3xddx(−1x2)−(−1x2)=x2ddx(2x3)+3x(2x3)+1x2=−6x2+6x2+1x2=1x2

q-337559.name: Question 3
q-337559.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=y,{f}_{1}=-xy,$ and ${f}_{0}=2y.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={e}^{2x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({e}^{2x}) & ={e}^{2x}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({e}^{2x})-x({e}^{2x})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{2x})+2({e}^{2x})^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{2x})-x{e}^{2x}\cdot 2{e}^{2x}+2{e}^{4x} \\  & ={e}^{2x}\cdot 4{e}^{2x}-2x{e}^{4x}+2{e}^{4x} \\  & =4{e}^{4x}-2x{e}^{4x}+2{e}^{4x} \\  & =6{e}^{4x}-2x{e}^{4x} \\  & =2{e}^{4x}(3-x)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

If D(y)=yd2ydx2−xydydx+2y2, then D(e2x)=

a
2e4x(3+x)
b
2e4x(1+3x)
c
2e4x(3−x)
d
2e4x(2−x)
e
2e4x(2+x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

D(y)=f2(x,y)d2ydx2+f1(x,y)dydx+f0(x,y)y with f2=y,f1=−xy, and f0=2y.

To compute D(y), we apply the definition of the operator D to the function y=e2x: D(e2x)=e2xd2dx2(e2x)−x(e2x)ddx(e2x)+2(e2x)2=e2xddx(2e2x)−xe2x⋅2e2x+2e4x=e2x⋅4e2x−2xe4x+2e4x=4e4x−2xe4x+2e4x=6e4x−2xe4x=2e4x(3−x)

q-337842.name: Question 4
q-337842.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=3{x}^{2},{f}_{1}=-x,$ and ${f}_{0}=-2.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(x-5) \\  & =(3{x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}-2)(x-5) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(x-5)-x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x-5)-2(x-5) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\cdot 0-x\cdot 1-2x+10 \\  & =10-3x\end{aligned}
$$

q-337849.name: Question 5
q-337849.worked_solution:
The given operator is a second-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={f}_{2}(x,y)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{f}_{1}(x,y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{f}_{0}(x,y)y
$$

with ${f}_{2}=xy,{f}_{1}=-y,$ and ${f}_{0}=4.$

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y={x}^{2}-3x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D({x}^{2}-3x) & =x({x}^{2}-3x)\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}({x}^{2}-3x)-({x}^{2}-3x)\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-3x)+4({x}^{2}-3x) \\  & =x({x}^{2}-3x)\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-3)-({x}^{2}-3x)(2x-3)+4({x}^{2}-3x) \\  & =x({x}^{2}-3x)\cdot 2-({x}^{2}-3x)(2x-3)+4({x}^{2}-3x) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+6{x}^{2}-9x+4{x}^{2}-12x \\  & =7{x}^{2}-21x \\  & =7x(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$
